panels.title: Emotion recognition with 10% labels
panels.subtitle: IEMOCAP · four emotions · 8–10 clients · mean of five runs
panels.finding: +7.22–10.28 UA points with the same 10% label budget across all four partitions.

takeaways: Unlabeled speech helps every tested partition, while full-label training remains stronger.
Unseen-speaker evaluation holds out sessions; overlapping-speaker scores assess a different setting.

sources.label: Table III · page 5
sources.location: Table III, PDF p. 5; all four partition rows and all three label/training settings. Evaluation protocol in Section IV and Table I, pp. 4–5.

notes: All 12 displayed means were checked visually against Table III in arXiv:2202.02611v1. Five full runs are performed per split; no SD, variance or confidence interval is supplied.
Row-wise self-training gains over the same 10%-label supervised baseline are 7.22, 10.28, 7.46 and 9.75 percentage points. These are absolute UA-point gains, not relative percentages.

Unseen speakers means leave-one-session-out (a session contains a dyad), not leave-one-speaker-out. Overlapping speakers uses five-fold 80:20 splits. Random partitions have 10 clients; per-speaker partitions have 8.
The paper’s Table II centralized-to-federated gaps and its prose disagree in ordering; neither those prose approximations nor a corrected threshold formula is introduced here.
No numerical or threshold-schedule edits were needed in data/insights/fedser.json.
